hook_text: 23 rows of 14 seats. Most people get 212. The hall actually holds 322. Here is the missing piece.
clip_script: School hall in Welkom. 23 rows, 14 seats a row. Quick guess: 20 times 10 is 200, 3 times 4 is 12, so 212? Wrong. Look at the hall. Split the rows: 20 and 3. Split each row: 10 seats and 4. That makes four blocks, not two. 20 rows of 10: 200. 20 rows of the 4 extra seats: 80. 3 rows of 10: 30. 3 rows of 4: 12. Add them: 322 seats. The two strips, 80 and 30, are what the quick guess forgot. Draw a grid, two across, two down, and every block gets a box. Estimate first: about 20 times 15, about 300. 322 fits. 212 does not. Four boxes, every time.
visual_style: Whiteboard hall grid splitting into four coloured blocks, each labelled with its product; a 2 by 2 grid filling cell by cell.
mood: Reveal of a common trap, then a satisfying fix.
pacing: The wrong answer first, the four-block picture, the grid filled fast, then the estimate check.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and multiply the rows and seats in your own classroom.
